chunks: And the Prophet, peace be upon him and his family, said:
Whoever is tested with judging should treat them equally in gestures and glances within the gathering.

key_terms.ابْتُلِيَ: is put to the test or charged with a serious responsibility
key_terms.الْإِشَارَةِ: gesturing or bodily indication toward one party
key_terms.الْمَجْلِسِ: the session or gathering in which judgment takes place
key_terms.بِالْقَضَاءِ: with judging or exercising judicial authority
key_terms.فَلْيُسَاوِ: then let him treat equally and without preference

ai.seo_question: How should a judge behave equally toward disputing parties in an Islamic court?
ai.summary: This hadith instructs a judge to maintain equality between litigants even in subtle outward conduct such as gestures, looks, and seating conduct in the session. It highlights that justice in Islam includes not only rulings themselves, but also visible impartiality in demeanor.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3242 - The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said:
"Whoever is tested with judging should treat them equally in gestures and glances within the gathering."
